kata.name: State-discovery drift and undeclared state - a documented target drift caught by an equation, and an undeclared state name refused at parse
kata.series_report: docs/ref/ploeh-grounding.md §6 candidate 4 (reverse state-machine kata); fixtures/katas/state-discovery/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-lgl.4
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: the drift is an executed equation violation on an unsampled cell; a transition naming an undeclared state is an executed construction rejection, recorded as a probe and never counted as a finding

expected.detail: cell Playing/pause declares target Stopped while its transition ends in Paused; the accepted equation cell_transition;to = cell_target emits an executed violation on that cell. The baseline sample omits Playing/pause
t_playing_stop maps to Ghost, a state not declared in State; the parser refuses the document (syntax), recorded as an executed construction probe, not a finding

commands: python3 prototype/state_discovery_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: baseline sample omits Playing/pause and Playing/stop
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/state-discovery/drift-target.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 1 violation
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/state-discovery/unknown-target.ct.json --json  # exit 1, syntax rejection (see probes)

probes.name: undeclared-target

equations.rationale: the documented transition starts in the cell's state
the documented transition fires on the cell's event
the documented transition ends in the cell's declared target

probes.observed: exit 1; code syntax; message: table `to` maps `t_playing_stop` to `Ghost`, which is not a row of `State` (line 70, column 27)

comparison.conventional_baseline: the frozen sample (five cells, omitting Playing/pause and Playing/stop) asserts every sampled cell and passes; both the drift and the undeclared name sit outside it.

baseline.artifact: prototype/state_discovery_baseline.py sha256:7d98b54bb65ea4e4c00962fc1d0e3e57ce19acb134f5d767b1177badd11fec3e (frozen transition-table sample; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: an undeclared target state is a finding
expressibility_gap.why: name resolution happens at parse: an undeclared state name is a syntax rejection (exit 1), never a finding; only null targets reach the dangling surface

procedure: 1. The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/state-discovery/ before any recorded run (README.md, faults.json); nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/state_discovery_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: frozen per-fixture samples of (state,event) cells asserting cell->transition, source/event/target agreement. Cells outside the sample are never inspected.

3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`, plus `catherine underconstraint --max-path-length 1 --json` where the discovery questions belong to the entry; the construction probe is the same binary refusing an unparseable document.

4. Witnesses were mapped to presentation elements cell:<State>/<Event>; unique_detections = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. Hypothesized underconstraint findings and executed construction rejections are recorded but never counted as detections.
5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; unique with an executed baseline arm = survived.
